subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway permanently add a separate pre-upgrade admission layer and three gateway.security settings, or should this hardening be integrated into the existing upgrade/origin/proxy policy without a parallel configuration surface?
rationale: This choice defines a public configuration contract and a pre-authentication network trust boundary; implementation correctness alone cannot establish the intended default and ownership policy.

options.title: Consolidate in upgrade handling
options.body: Move the checks into the HTTP upgrade handler, reuse canonical locality and raw-header parsing, and retain opt-in compatibility defaults.

options.title: Approve the proposed boundary
options.body: Keep verifyClient and gateway.security after explicitly approving the defaults, documenting upgrade impact, and obtaining comprehensive live handshake proof.

options.title: Pause for origin-policy alignment
options.body: Defer this PR until the adjacent origin-pattern and browser-origin direction is settled, then submit one coherent admission policy.

recommendation.title: Consolidate in upgrade handling
recommendation.body: Move the checks into the HTTP upgrade handler, reuse canonical locality and raw-header parsing, and retain opt-in compatibility defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history and PR discussion consistently route Gateway handshake, locality, and browser-origin policy through this person.
